svg.font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: A commercial HVAC account and its stakeholders, and the contact rules that protect it
svg.desc: A two-panel diagram. The left panel, headed One account, several people, lists four people at a single commercial account and how each is graded. A director of facilities is a named decision-maker and may be contacted. A named property manager for the site is a named decision-maker and may be contacted. A maintenance supervisor is a named contact who routes but does not decide. A general info address or main line is a generic front door and is never treated as decision-maker access. The right panel, headed Four rules enforced in code, states that one person's opt-out suppresses the entire organisation; an open conversation stops a cold message to a colleague; message limits are counted across the whole account rather than per person; and an account belongs to one contractor and is never worked for two at once. A closing band states that a general inbox is never verified decision-maker access.
svg.text: A commercial account is not a contact
One building portfolio holds several people. Reaching one of them changes what may be sent to the rest.
One account · several people
Director of facilities
NAMED DECISION-MAKER
Decides the vendor. May be contacted.
Property manager for the site
NAMED DECISION-MAKER
Decides, or routes to who does.
Maintenance supervisor
NAMED CONTACT
Routes a request. Does not decide.
A general inbox or main line
GENERIC FRONT DOOR
Never decision-maker access.
Four rules enforced in code
1 · One opt-out stops the account
If any one person opts out, the whole
organisation is suppressed — not just them.
2 · An open thread stops a cold one
While a conversation is live, no colleague
receives a cold first message.
3 · Limits count across the account
Message ceilings and spacing are counted
over all stakeholders, never per person.
4 · One account, one contractor
An account is never worked for two
clients at the same time.
A general inbox is never verified decision-maker access
A message is not sent to a person the record cannot evidence.
